config_name: Galaxy Book4 15.6 — Intel Core 7 150U (Raptor Lake), Iris Xe, 16GB, 512GB, 15.6" FHD IPS

battery.notes: Raptor Lake U is the least efficient chip in this lineup; ~8-9h light use.

price.notes: Reg $1,729 / clearance $1,199 (BBY-verified 2026-11-24). Notable prev-gen value pick at this price. SKU 18904449.

offers.name: Samsung Galaxy Book 4 15.6" FHD Intel Core 7 150U 16GB 512GB Windows 11 Silver

reviews.quote: Almost entirely uninspiring: stylish and well-made, but undermined by a low-quality display, which has no place in an £899 laptop.

praises: $1,199 clearance for a 15.6" 16GB/512GB name-brand laptop — strong budget-office value at BBY
Core 7 150U (10-core) handles everyday multitasking fine and stays quiet
Numeric keypad and big screen for spreadsheets at an entry price
Slim ~1.6 kg chassis for a 15.6-incher, decent build for the price
Galaxy Quick Share / phone link features retained from the premium lines
complaints: 2024 Raptor Lake platform — no NPU, not Copilot+, aging quickly
Dim 300-nit FHD 16:9 IPS panel, 60 Hz, non-touch
Iris Xe struggles with anything beyond casual games
Samsung bloatware heavier on the budget SKUs
Coil-whine reports on the bundled charger across the Book4 line

design_philosophy: The Book4 15.6 is the outgoing mainstream tier — Raptor Lake U silicon, a big boring FHD screen, and everything a home office needs without a single premium flourish. At $1,199 clearance it becomes exactly what Samsung's 15.6 line has always been for: an unexciting, comfortable, big-keyboard value machine, and the notable prev-gen pick of the CA Galaxy Book range.
rating_notes: Synthesized per SHARED-galaxy-book.md (honest null on pro coverage). vs Book5 15.6: older Raptor Lake = −1 battery, ai_ml 1.5 (no NPU), similar everything else; clearance price is its whole story. Image URL best-guess BBY CDN pattern.
